resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO) - Resale
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Fair Lawn Construction Code Official (Building Department resale-CCO inspectors; Zoning Dept phone on the form)
resale_co.lead_time: The ordinance says the CCO is issued or denied within 10 days of filing the application. Inspections are 12 pm to 4 pm.
resale_co.valid_for: One year from the date of issuance, provided there is no material change in the physical status of the premises
requirements: Applies to one- and two-family dwellings on any transfer of title (exempt: 3+ family buildings, deed corrections, spouse and parent/child or grandparent/grandchild transfers, new construction, estate distributions, receivers/trustees, quitclaims to quiet title)

Visual inspection by the Construction Code Official (who may refer to subcode officials, the Water Department and the Department of Health) covering sidewalks, electrical service, plumbing, heating and ventilation, building exterior, fences, driveways and other hazards

Resale checklist also covers walkways, debris, oil tank, railings, accessory structures, sprinklers, water valve certificate, water heater, sump pump, gas pipe, handrails, stairs, renovations, fire certificate and open permits
Water service valves before and after the meter must be working ball valves, signed off by the Department of Public Works (Ordinance 241.24)
Smoke alarm certificate from the Fire Prevention Bureau
Additions or construction done without permits must be legalized

fees.label: CCO for one- or two-family dwelling, initial inspection plus one follow-up
fees.quote: For an initial and one follow-up inspection: $175.

fees.label: Each subsequent CCO inspection for the same applicant
fees.quote: For each subsequent inspection for the same applicant: $50.

fees.label: Additional certified copy of the CCO
fees.quote: For issuance of additional certified copies of the certificate of continued occupancy: $5.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Complete the Borough's Application for Certificate of Continued Occupancy-Resale (owner, buyer, both attorneys, closing date, whether the buyer will occupy) and pay the fee; the form says to call the Zoning Dept at 201-794-5308 and that a missed appointment counts as the first inspection. Have the DPW water valve letter signed and get the Fire Prevention Bureau smoke alarm certificate. If violations remain, the Construction Code Official may allow closing when the purchaser certifies in writing that violations will be corrected and a repair escrow is set up.
resale_co.contact_title: Building and Zoning Official (CCO form lists Zoning Dept 201-794-5308)

evidence.quote: Transfer of title to real property in the Borough of Fair Lawn containing a building or permanent structure of any kind.
This section does not apply to the sale of a "multiple-family dwelling" which is defined, for the purpose of this section, as property which contains three or more dwelling units.
All certificates of continued occupancy shall be issued or denied within 10 days of the filing of the application.
A certificate of continued occupancy shall be deemed valid for one year from the date of issuance, provided that there is no material change in the physical status of the premises.
No owner shall permit the sale of premises covered by this section unless the requisite certificate of continued occupancy has been issued.
For an initial and one follow-up inspection: $175.
For each subsequent inspection for the same applicant: $50.
The fee for a certificate of continued occupancy shall be $175.
The Building Department also houses the zoning board of adjustment, property maintenance and resale-cco inspectors.
Richard Bolan - Building and Zoning Official
INSPECTION – PLUS 1 RE-INSPECTION FEE: $175.00
CERTIFICATE WILL BE VALID FOR ONE YEAR FROM DATE OF ISSUANCE

resale_co.notes: Fair Lawn Code Section 125-80.1 requires a Certificate of Continued Occupancy on any transfer of title of a one- or two-family dwelling, with listed exemptions, and bars the sale until it is issued. Fee is in Chapter 94 (and repeated in Section 85-3F). The Borough's application, checklist and smoke flyer PDFs are scanned images, so their quotes cannot be text-matched. Section 85-3F(4) also sets a $50 fee for an optional 'code letter at the time of resale or when refinancing'; that is a records letter, not the CCO.

requirements: At least one 10 year sealed smoke alarm on each level including the basement, within 10 feet of each entrance to a sleeping area (or inside each sleeping area), and near the stairway on levels without a sleeping area
Hardwired smoke detectors from original construction or rehabilitation must be kept operational; wireless detectors do not meet code unless installed by permit or variance
Combination smoke/CO alarms must be 10 year sealed battery units
Carbon monoxide alarm on each level that has a bedroom (battery, hard-wired or plug-in; table-top models not acceptable)
Two-family homes: 10 year sealed smoke detector outside each doorway in common stairwells and hallways, and a smoke alarm at the foot of the stairs in each separate basement
Secondary power source caution label within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and meter if the home has a generator, solar panels or battery storage
Fire extinguisher (ordinance fee title still lists it)

authorities.lead_time: Fee depends on how far in advance the inspection is scheduled. The certificate is good for six months.

fire_cert.notes: The ordinance (Chapter 94, amended through Ord. 2759-2025) sets $90 and a $50 reinspection; the Bureau's flyer (dated July 1, 2020) says the fee varies from $90.00 to $125.00 depending on notice, so the exact middle and short-notice tiers are not published. The fee title still names the fire extinguisher, which P.L.2025, c.19 removed from the sale certificate in February 2025; the March 4, 2025 CO and secondary power source flyer does not list an extinguisher. The flyers are scanned image PDFs. Fire official email is from the NJ DCA directory.

other_items.label: Water meter valve inspection (DPW)
other_items.detail: Under Ordinance 241.24 the water service valves before and after the meter must be working ball valves; call DPW at 201-794-5326 or 201-794-5304 for an inspection and give the signed letter to the Building Department.

other_items.label: Open permits and unpermitted work
other_items.detail: Additions or construction found without permits must be legalized before the CCO; the checklist records open building, plumbing, electrical and fire permits.

other_items.label: Optional code letter
other_items.detail: A $50 code letter at resale or refinancing is available from the Construction office (separate from the CCO).
